---
title: "Final Project Workflow"
---

## Separate preparation from presentation

Use one reproducible script to clean and validate the data, then save a single
named object as RDS:

```{r}
#| eval: false
analysis_data <- raw_data |>
  # cleaning steps
  identity()

stopifnot(!anyNA(analysis_data$key))
saveRDS(analysis_data, "data/processed/analysis_data.rds")
```

Load it explicitly in each page that needs it:

```{r}
#| eval: false
analysis_data <- readRDS("data/processed/analysis_data.rds")
```

RDS is preferable here to `.RData` because `readRDS()` returns one object whose
name you choose. `load()` can silently add several pre-named objects to the
environment.

## Save a static chart

```{r}
#| eval: false
ggsave(
  "outputs/main-chart.png",
  plot = main_chart,
  width = 8,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)
```

Insert it with alt text:

```markdown
![A concise description of the chart's main pattern.](outputs/main-chart.png)
```

## Choose geometry from the data structure

Use a line only when the x variable has a meaningful order, usually time. For a
relationship between two unordered numeric variables, use points:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = hp, y = qsec)) +
  geom_point(color = "#1769AA") +
  labs(
    title = "Quarter-mile time and horsepower",
    x = "Horsepower",
    y = "Quarter-mile time (seconds)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Connecting cars with a line would imply a sequence that does not exist.

## Final project checklist

- raw data preserved unchanged;
- source, access date, and terms recorded;
- grain stated before and after aggregation;
- cleaned data regenerated by a script;
- denominators explicit;
- joins audited for unmatched and duplicated keys;
- at least three machine-readable checks;
- chart values reconciled with a table;
- causal language supported by appropriate evidence;
- methods and limitations written for readers; and
- the full site renders after restarting R.
